chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who had a debt due from another man, but the debtor was lost, and it was not known whether he was alive or dead, and no heir or relative or country was known for him. He (the Imam) said, 'Seek him out.' He said, 'That has taken a long time, so shall I give it in charity?' He said, 'Seek him out.'

key_terms.أَصَّدَّقُ بِهِ: shall I give it in charity

ai.seo_question: What should a creditor do with a debt if the debtor is lost and has no known heirs?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) insists that the creditor must continue searching for the lost debtor (*mafqud*) rather than distributing the debt amount as charity, even if the search becomes prolonged. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that the debtor’s right to the principal remains intact until their death or return is confirmed, preventing premature appropriation of their wealth by the creditor. It highlights the meticulous care taken in preserving individual property rights within the framework of *fiqh al-duyun* (jurisprudence of debts).
